title: Tech that changed the world

slides.title: Tradeoffs everywhere
slides.text: Technology is neither all good nor all bad. Every advance has a benefit for someone and a cost for someone else.
slides.alt: Would you rather: a game that is free but shows ads, or a game you pay for once with no ads?

focus.cue: Free: a benefit for players, ads the cost
Paid once: no ads, but it costs money

slides.title: Automation
slides.text: Automation means a machine does a task people used to do. It changes jobs more than it erases them: someone builds the robots, and someone fixes them.
slides.alt: Would you rather have a job building robots, or a job fixing robots?

slides.title: Self-checkout
slides.text: Look at both sides: what it does for daily life, and what it does to jobs.

slides.title: Hidden costs
slides.text: A map app saves time, but you may stop learning your way around. Driverless cars might prevent some crashes and change drivers' jobs.
slides.alt: Would you rather: a map app that picks your route, or a paper map and your own choices?

focus.cue: A paper map: you learn the way yourself

words.means: a benefit in one place, a cost in another
a machine doing a task people used to do
control over who knows things about you
the kind of work a person does over many years

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Pick one technology you used today. Name one benefit for everyday life and one cost for someone's job or privacy. Then talk about it.
slides.alt: Would you rather: a voice helper that knows everything, or one that never listens unless you press a button?

focus.cue: Benefit: a helper that knows everything
Privacy: one that only listens on a press

talk: Which invention would you un-invent for a week? Who would be better off, and who would be worse off?
